newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed, deferreds up in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed, deferreds up in thin trade.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled mixed with deferred contracts edging higher in lackluster volume, traders said.
"We were trading so thinly in here that any buying allowed our market to bounce," a trader said at the close.
Traders said the higher move in July and September wheat came in part because of concerns about dryness in western Kansas and eastern Colorado.
"Part of it may have been the dryness talk, which I'd keep in the back of my mind," another trader said. "We'll know more after the state crop reports (are released later Monday)."
Wheat had been weak early on spillover pressure from CBOT soybeans, which sagged amid improved planting conditions in the U.S. Midwest.
KCBT wheat settled 1-1/4 cents per bushel lower to 2-1/2 cents higher, with May down 1-1/4 cent at $4.12. July gained two cents to close at $3.85-1/2.
FIMAT and Prudential Securities each bought at least one million May bushels, and traders guessed this was linked to commission house activity. General Mills sold one million May.
